title: Privacy-Preserving Deep JSCC for Wireless Image Transmission Using Keyed Orthonormal Latent Scrambling
content: Deep joint source–channel coding (JSCC) enables learned wireless image transmission while exposing transmitted representations to unintended receivers. Protecting these representations requires a reproducible keyed interface and an evaluation that connects legitimate  image quality with reconstruction and semantic leakage. We integrate a packet-specific, keyed orthonormal transform with deep JSCC, establish its exact legitimate-channel equivalence under additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN), and assess confidentiality through independently trained codecs, adaptive attackers and resource-controlled transmission experiments. Across six codecs trained in three paired seed comparisons, the legitimate receiver achieves a valid-window structural similarity index measure of 0.8365–0.8401 at a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of 12 dB, while validation-selected reconstruction attackers at 20 dB obtain 0.1306–0.1307 against an image-prior baseline of 0.1307; selected semantic classification accuracy averages 9.59–10.26% over repeated keys and channel draws. These findings establish a substantial measured separation between legitimate reconstruction and the information recovered by the evaluated attackers, with explicit computation and metadata costs.
